A1.justification: Both PDFs present GestureLSM and contain readable main text, equations, nine figures, three tables, and Appendices A–E. Text and visual inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original BEAT2 evaluations, a 20-participant user study, ablations in Tables 2–3, and training analyses in Figure 9.

after.justification: v3 retains the original BEAT2 results, user study, ablations, and training analyses, which independently establish empirical content.

M1.justification: The RVQ representation, spatial and temporal attention, latent shortcut procedure, and beta timestep sampling are unchanged. Appendix B changes the codebook-reset attribution but specifies no different algorithmic operation.

E1.justification: Both versions retain BEAT2 co-speech gesture generation, body-only and body-plus-face evaluation, and the same avatar-video demonstrations. No dataset, population, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all nine baselines, including EMAGE, MambaTalk, SynTalker, and DiffSHEG. The user-study and ablation comparator sets also remain unchanged; newly cited works are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The EMAGE data split, evaluation metrics, eight-step default sampling, training budgets, and A100 timing setup are retained. The user study still uses 20 participants and 320 videos with randomized presentation and ratings from 1 to 5.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same module, architecture, sampling, guidance, feature-fusion, and representation ablations. The denoising analysis, qualitative examples, and Appendix E training analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 7 retains the same MOS error bars, whose statistical meaning remains unspecified. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged, including GestureLSM's Table 1 FGD of 4.088 and AIST of 0.039. Figure 7 retains MOS values of 4.16, 4.27, and 4.32 for GestureLSM; the other plots and qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and the accompanying quantization, attention, flow-matching, shortcut, beta-distribution, and metric formulations are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about coherent full-body gestures, spatial-temporal interaction modeling, improved flow matching, state-of-the-art BEAT2 performance, and real-time generation.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations for spatial-temporal coordination and beta sampling, and the argument that beat constancy should be assessed relative to ground truth. Appendix E's interpretation is preserved across its changed page break; no substantive limitation is added.

D1.justification: Appendix B changes the cited source for codebook resets from MoMask to Contextual Gesture, revising implementation guidance without explaining different reset mechanics. Hyperparameters, hardware, training durations, and project-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Nine references are added, including SemGes, Intentional Gesture, EraseAnything, DCTdiff, and OFTSR, within existing related-work citation groups. The previous references remain, and the substantive research-positioning argument is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes the repeated supplementary title, fixes duplicated punctuation, and makes several appendix pointers less specific, including removing the Table 3e pointer in Section 3.3. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds page numbers and introduces limited bibliography and appendix reflow, including moving the start of Appendix E onto PDF page 12 after removing the supplementary title block. Figure designs and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, empirical evidence in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–9, and scientific interpretations are unchanged. Expanded citations, revised reset-source attribution, and small layout and cross-reference edits leave the paper's overall technical clarity and evidential support materially the same.
